sentences.text: This Writ Petition by the erstwhile owner of the land in question seeks to lay a challenge to the acquisition proceedings initiated vide Preliminary Notification dated 4.8.1988 gazetted on 31.1.1991 followed by the Final Notification dated 14.1.1992 and culminating into the award dated 30.9.1993.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner vehemently argues that the possession having not been taken over till date, the acquisition should be set at naught under the provisions of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He hastens to add that the compensation amount received by his client should be remitted back immediately.

2. Learned AGA on request having accepted notice for the official Respondents, opposes the Petition contending that the challenge has been highly belated; the possession of the land having been taken over long back, even the compensation has admittedly been paid to the land owner/khatedar as is evidenced by the acknowledgement of receipt dated 11.04.1998 at Annexure-M to the Petition.
So contending, he seeks dismissal of the Writ Petition.
3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court is broadly in agreement with the submission of learned AGA appearing for the Respondents.
Firstly, the challenge is highly belated and decades have rolled since the acquisition.
No plausible explanation has been offered for the long delay brooked in approaching the Writ Court.

sentences.text: because the entries in the Revenue Records still continue in the name of the land owner, is of no avail when admittedly, the compensation has been received by the land owner/khatedar and a copy of the acknowledgement has been produced by the Petitioner herself.

The Apex Court in GOVERNMENT OF NCT OF DELHI vs. MOHD. ZUBAIR (2023) 1 SCC 174 has observed that once compensation has been accepted unreservedly, the same amounts to acquiescing in the acquisition and therefore, the challenge that too at a belated stage, is unsustainable.

entities.text: GOVERNMENT OF NCT OF DELHI vs. MOHD. ZUBAIR (2023) 1 SCC 174
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. The vehement submission of learned counsel for the Petitioner that once the possession is not taken within a period of five years from the date the 2013 Act came into force, his client is entitled to have the acquisition voided, is contrary to INDORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY vs.
MANOHARLAL, (2020) 8 SCC 129 and therefore, the benefit contemplated u/s 24(2) thereof,
cannot be availed by the Petitioner.
In view of the above, Writ Petition being devoid of merits, is liable to be dismissed and accordingly,
it is, costs having been made easy.
Sd/-
